verdict.rationale: Zulip ships a first-party interactive bot framework: you can run custom or existing bots that react to messages, and keep them running persistently via the Zulip Botserver. That gives event-driven background automation, but it requires writing or deploying bot code and is limited to reacting to messages. missing for 10: no-code automation builder, recurring/scheduled triggers, AI/agentic automation features, depth of Botserver docs, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Zulip’s API has a powerful framework for interactive bots that react to messages in Zulip. You can write and run a custom bot, or run an existing Zulip bot.
Eventually, you’ll probably want to run it in a production environment where it’ll stay up, by deploying it on a server using the Zulip Botserver.
